architecture.summary: PyJWT is a Python implementation of RFC 7519, enabling developers to encode and decode JSON Web Tokens (JWTs). It supports multiple cryptographic algorithms, JSON Web Keys (JWKs), and JWKS client retrieval with caching.

modules.name: jwt.api_jwt
modules.purpose: Provides the high-level PyJWT interface for encoding, decoding, and validating JSON Web Tokens.

modules.name: jwt.api_jws
modules.purpose: Implements JSON Web Signature (JWS) operations for signing and verifying token payloads.

modules.name: jwt.api_jwk
modules.purpose: Handles JSON Web Keys (JWKs) and JWK Sets for cryptographic key management.

modules.name: jwt.algorithms
modules.purpose: Implements various signing and hashing algorithms such as HMAC, RSA, ECDSA, and EdDSA using the cryptography library.

modules.name: jwt.jwks_client
modules.purpose: Provides a client to fetch and cache signing keys from a remote JWKS endpoint.

modules.name: jwt.exceptions
modules.purpose: Defines custom exceptions for decoding, signature verification, and validation failures.

modules.name: jwt.utils
modules.purpose: Contains helper utility functions for base64url encoding/decoding and signature conversions.

modules.name: jwt.jwk_set_cache
modules.purpose: Manages caching layers for JWK sets to prevent redundant network requests.
